A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVPA, MVPFormer, and SWEC research. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, algorithms, and Appendices A–G are readable and matchable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original iEEG prediction, seizure detection, Brain TreeBank decoding, time-series benchmarking, and computational experiments, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional attention-component ablations, noise-robustness experiments, and computational comparisons.

M1.justification: The three-component MVPA mechanism, FlashMVPA implementation, wavelet encoder, decoder architecture, contrastive pre-training, and LoRA fine-tuning remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–6. The new component variants are experimental ablations; channel selection changes the evaluation setup.

E1.justification: V3 adds a controlled corruption scenario using white Gaussian noise on SWEC recordings (Appendix G.14). The underlying datasets and tasks remain: SWEC, MAYO, FNUSA, Brain TreeBank, and the existing forecasting and classification benchmarks.

E2.justification: V3 adds standalone BrainBERT comparisons for SWEC and Brain TreeBank, distinct from the previously reported PopT using BrainBERT representations. The computational comparison expands from MVPA versus FlashMVPA to include naive self-attention, FlashAttention 2, and Nystromformer (Appendix A.7, Tables 8–12).

E3.justification: The main SWEC evaluation changes from manual selection of approximately 30–50 channels to automatic selection targeting 32 channels (Section 5.1 and Appendix E.1). New protocols include injected noise at 30–60 dB SNR and component-removal forecasting experiments. The original training split, training budget, and forecasting horizons remain.

E4.justification: V3 adds content-only, time-only, channel-only, and no-attention ablations on three forecasting datasets (Section 6.3, Appendix G.18), plus controlled noise robustness tests. Channel-selection analysis now compares automatic, manual, and all-channel evaluation. Earlier model-scaling, data-scaling, connectivity, and pre-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 adds per-subject Kappa columns labeled 95% CI, including for retained results such as the pre-training ablation. The existing estimation procedure using 300 sampled segments and 250 iterations remains unchanged. Increased training-run counts and the confidence-interval construction method are not documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes MVPFormer's SWEC Kappa/F1 from 0.57/0.56 to 0.61/0.59 under revised channel selection, so this is not a same-setting performance gain. Computational measurements are replaced, and BrainBERT, component-ablation, and noise results are added; Table 31 reports Kappa 0.58 at 60 dB and 0.12 at 30 dB. Some appendix subject entries also change, while existing forecasting, Brain TreeBank, MAYO, and FNUSA scores are retained.

T1.justification: V3 introduces the channel-ranking definition r_C = var(C)/(1 + kurt(C)) in Equation 10. The existing MVPA decomposition, complexity arguments, relative-shifting derivations, and structured-dropout formula remain unchanged. Expanded algebraic explanation does not introduce a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and claims: MVPA, the MVPFormer foundation model, the SWEC release, expert-level seizure detection, and competitive general time-series performance. Updated scores and clearer wording about downstream fine-tuning do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting component benefits to channel richness, motivating contrastive loss through L2-collapse concerns, and interpreting noise-induced false positives. It qualifies v2's assertion that absolute electrode positions carry no information. The data-quality discussion and cautions about automated clinical reliance and model use are removed, although data-scaling limitations and dataset-use restrictions remain in the appendices.

D1.justification: V3 specifies channel selection using the first 30 minutes, percentile filters, a ranking formula, and a fallback selection rule. It also documents bfloat16, 12 heads, and disabled GQA for computational benchmarking, without establishing that these were changed from previously used settings. Core architectural details, training resources, and code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion expands to space-time mixing, ViViT, STNDT, and additional electrode-location and iEEG dataset literature. References supporting the removed data-quality and broader-impact discussion disappear. These changes refine the existing positioning around simultaneous temporal/spatial attention and independence from electrode coordinates.

P1.justification: Substantial restructuring moves architecture and preprocessing explanations into appendices, promotes general time-series evaluation to a separate section, and reorders appendix analyses. Ethics and reproducibility statements reorganize the ending, while the former limitations and broader-impact sections disappear. Much underlying prose is retained.

P2.justification: The combined iEEG results table is split into separate seizure and Brain TreeBank tables. Numerous appendix tables gain confidence-interval columns, and new computational, noise, and component-ablation tables are introduced. The standalone main-text Kappa plot and Brant-2 distribution plot are removed, while retained figures and tables are repositioned within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: Replacing subjective channel selection with a specified automatic procedure improves reproducibility, while component ablations and broader computational comparisons strengthen assessment of the central design. These gains are tempered by unspecified confidence-interval construction, removed clinical-use cautions, and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 36 now lists 50 subjects under a 40-subject caption. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
